headline: Complete — 3,260 tracks analyzed and 124 harmonically-sequenced playlists built and pushed to the Walkman (after recovering from a playlist-build crash).
insights: Analysis done: 3,260 tracks with BPM, Camelot key, energy, structure and timbre — only 3 decode failures (0.09%) across the entire 71 GB library. Device stayed rock-solid the whole ~2.5 hours.
124 playlists built — 22 micro-genre vibe sets + 102 BPM-band crates — all sequenced by energy arc + Camelot harmonic mixing. Arc split is healthy: 38 hype · 51 journey · 35 soul.

The micro-split works now. Atlanta Trap → Hard (238, hype) vs Melodic (268, soul); Opium Rage → Hard (215, hype) vs Melodic (38); Toronto → Uptempo (97, hype) vs Late Night (237, soul) — the energy-driven scene carving the library asked for.

Final shape of the collection: house-forward (829 tracks at 120–129 BPM vs 496 trap), 34% major-key, median energy 0.54 — a groove-first crate with a hard trap/rage wing. Opium Rage is the single most energetic family (median 0.72).

Recovered from two real bugs mid-flight: a live-server hang under DB write-locks (fixed with WAL) and a playlist-build crash on the BPM-band naming (fixed + rebuilt from the DB in ~90s, no re-analysis needed). The unreliable vocal detector was de-weighted so it didn't corrupt sequencing.
